messages:
marta: Kicking off a small canary: introducing the 'token-hunch' lookahead heuristic on the 12B quant candidate. 2% traffic, cpu+gpu mixed pool.

sam: Nice. Quick remind — what's the heuristic threshold and fallback?

marta: threshold: entropy_delta > 0.9 over next 8 steps OR softmax peak > 0.7. If triggered, do speculative lookahead for up to 16 tokens, else regular decoder. Fallback to base model if latency > 250ms p95.

jin: Rough question — how are you measuring quality for this run? Which eval buckets?

marta: We're running parallel evals on a small holdout: HellaSwag subset (300 items), OpenQA dev (500 items), and a code generation microbench (50 snippets). Also tracking token-level KL and next-token accuracy against high-precision baseline.

sam: Can you paste the curl we used for canary routing? Want to replicate locally.

marta: Sure — using the internal canary route: 
```
curl -X POST https://api-canary.redwood.int/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-12b-quant-tokenhunch-canary","route":"canary:2%","prompt":"<PROMPT>","stream":false}'
```

jin: Any first-pass numbers? Latency and fail rates?

marta: Early telemetry from 1h: p50 ~ 95ms (baseline 110ms), p95 ~ 230ms (baseline 240ms). Cost per 1k tokens is ~8% lower due to fewer decode steps. Error rate 0.4% vs baseline 0.2% (HTTP 500s from a small edge allocator mismatch).

sam: Quality tradeoffs? Anything notable on HellaSwag or QA?

marta: HellaSwag accuracy down 1.6% absolute vs full-precision baseline. On OpenQA exact-match down 0.9%. Code microbench — no measurable regression (small sample). Token-level KL up 0.03 on average for generated tokens where heuristic triggered.

jin: 1.6% HellaSwag is borderline. Do we know if regressions correlate with specific prompt patterns?

marta: Early flags suggest longer-context prompts with rhetorical multi-sentences tend to trigger lookahead and produce slightly more generic outputs. Also prompts with many options/choices show biggest drop.

sam: Can we flip the heuristic to be more conservative (longer entropy window, higher delta) and re-run?

marta: Yep — planning two micro-variants: token-hunch-a (entropy_delta > 1.2, lookahead max 12) and token-hunch-b (only trigger on seq_len > 64). Run both in parallel at 0.5% each.

deploy-bot: deploy event: rwd-12b-quant-tokenhunch-canary -> 2% traffic (started 1738897708). Instances: 12 pods.

jin: For evaluation methodology: propose we compute per-example delta in log-prob of gold token and bucket by prompt length and prompt type (instruction vs QA vs choice). That should tell us if loss concentrates on particular patterns.

marta: Agreed. I'll attach per-example diffs to the canary dashboard. Also adding a small human eval for ~100 HellaSwag failure cases to check if drop is spurious.

sam: Also add uncertainty coverage: fraction of tokens where lookahead triggered. If a tiny % of tokens cause most regressions, maybe we can gate triggers by token-importance (e.g., nouns/propernouns).

jin: One more: measure degeneracy metrics — repetition rate and palette collapse (vocab entropy) for sequences where we triggered lookahead.

marta: Good call. I'll add repetition@k and vocab-entropy curves.

marta: Next steps: 1) Run token-hunch-a and b at 0.5% each for 4h; 2) collect per-example log-prob deltas, KL, repetition metrics; 3) human review of worst 100 HellaSwag diffs; 4) tweak threshold or restrict to seq_len>64.

sam: If we can get quality within 0.5% HellaSwag and maintain ~5-10% cost win, this is worth iterating. Else rollback. :thumbsup:

jin: I'll shadow the canary telemetry and start the per-example aggregation job. Ping me on the thread when the two micro variants are up.

marta: Will do. Thanks all. :rocket:
